name: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah
nameAr: سفيان بن عُيينة بن أبي عمران الهلالي

nisbas.en: al-Hilali (Banu Hilal ibn Amir, by clientage)

mawla: Banu Hilal (al-Hilali mawlahum). Ibn Sa'd: mawla of Banu Abdullah ibn Ruwayba of Hilal ibn Amir; also reported as mawla of Muhammad ibn Muzahim, brother of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim; al-Ijli: mawla of Mis'ar ibn Kidam (rejected by Ibn Hajar in Tabaqat al-Mudallisin)

deathVariants.authority: al-Waqidi: Saturday 1 Rajab 198; Ibn al-Salah affirmed 198; the Taqrib gives Rajab 198
deathVariants.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib (Hyderabad ed.) 4/117-122, OpenITI transcription of Shamela 3310, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenITI/0875AH/master/data/0852IbnHajarCasqalani/0852IbnHajarCasqalani.TahdhibTahdhib/0852IbnHajarCasqalani.TahdhibTahdhib.Shamela0003310-ara2; Taqrib al-Tahdhib, entry 2451, https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تقريب_التهذيب/حرف_السين_المهملة/ذكر_من_اسمه_سعيد_(إلى_آخر_حرف_السين)

deathVariants.authority: recorded as an alternative in Shamela's narrator record (no classical authority named there)

taqrib.ar: ثقة حافظ فقيه إمام حجة، إلا أنه تغير حفظه بأخرة، وكان ربما دلّس لكن عن الثقات
taqrib.en: Reliable, a hadith master, jurist, imam and proof; however his memory changed late in life, and he would sometimes transmit with an ambiguous formula, though only from reliable narrators.

verdicts.ar: كان يدلس ولا يدلس إلا عن ثقة متقن
verdicts.en: He would use the ambiguous formula, but only over a reliable, precise narrator; something found in no one else, and wherever he did it the same report is found with his hearing stated.

verdicts.ar: وأنا أستبعد هذا الكلام من القطان وأعده غلطًا من ابن عمار
verdicts.en: On the report that his memory failed in 197: “I consider this far-fetched from al-Qattan and count it an error by Ibn Ammar”, since al-Qattan died in Safar 198, just as the pilgrims were returning with news from the Hijaz, leaving no time to learn of a change and testify to it.
verdicts.source: Mizan al-I'tidal, as quoted in al-Ightibat no. 44

tadlis.type: tadlis al-isnad, only over reliable narrators
tadlis.source: Ibn Hajar, Tabaqat al-Mudallisin, rank 2, no. 52, https://shamela.ws/book/1186/29
tadlis.note: «كان يدلس لكن لا يدلس إلا عن ثقة، وادعى ابن حبان بأن ذلك كان خاصا، ووصفه النسائي وغيره بالتدليس». Ibn Hajar rejects al-Burhan al-Halabi's second entry for a "Sufyan ibn Uyaynah al-Hilali, mawla of Mis'ar, worthless" as a confusion: Ibn Uyaynah is the mawla of Banu Hilal.

flags.label: Occasional tadlis, tolerated
flags.detail: Ibn Hajar places him in the second rank of Tabaqat al-Mudallisin (entry 52): narrators whose ambiguous “from” the imams accepted because of their stature and because they only did it over reliable people. In this chain he says “narrated to us”, so the link is explicit and the question does not arise. Ibn Hajar notes that in Abu Dharr al-Harawi's recension of the Sahih this link reads “from”.

flags.label: Late change of memory, disputed
flags.detail: Yahya al-Qattan is reported to have said Sufyan's memory became confused in 197 AH. Al-Dhahabi rejected the report on the dates; Ibn Hajar accepted it. Either way, al-Humaydi was “the firmest of people in Ibn Uyaynah”, so the question does not touch this chain. The record exists so that it can be asked.

bio: One of the two great Sufyans of the second century, a Kufan who settled in Makkah and taught there for decades. Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, al-Humaydi and Ibn Ma'in were among his students.
